# CVR Engineering — Phase 1 Baseline: Findings

**Deliverable:** `model/CVR_Model_Phase1_Baseline.xlsx` (generated by `scripts/build_phase1_workbook.py`)
**Sources:** 2026 rate sheet + CVR/EPC KPI report (week ending 7/11/2026), both in `data/`
**Status:** Baseline complete and tied out; open items listed below gate Phase 1 exit

---

## What the workbook contains

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| README | Purpose, color key (blue = input, orange = assumption to confirm), sources |
| Assumptions | Global inputs; fringe load, overhead allocation, and interest basis flagged TBD from finance |
| Rates | The 2026 rate card and billing policies |
| Roster & Hours | 13 people with classifications, YTD hours, utilization vs per-person targets, and billable value at card rates |
| Baseline P&L | CVR monthly actuals vs budget, Jan–May 2026, with derived Cost of Sales and OpEx lines |
| HWC EPC Baseline | The EPC line's Jan–May financials for context |
| Realization | The rate-card gap analysis and a utilization × realization annualized-revenue grid |
| Checks & Open Items | Automatic tie-outs to the KPI report and the open-question list |

All six tie-outs reconcile to the KPI report: CVR revenue $426.7K, GP $76.8K, net −$304.7K; EPC revenue $1,172.4K, net −$2,109.3K; billable hours 4,747.

## Findings

**1. The blended rate card for the current mix is $154/hr; CVR is realizing ~$114/hr (≈74%).**
This refines the plan's earlier ~$90/hr estimate, which ignored the timing mismatch between the hours data (through 7/11) and financials (through 5/31). Adjusting hours to the Jan–May window: ~3,736 billable hours × $154.47 blended card = **$577K of card-rate value vs $426.7K recognized — a ~$150K YTD gap (26%)**. The Realization tab has an input block to decompose the gap into billing lag / write-offs / internal transfer pricing once finance answers; internal transfer pricing is the primary suspect.

**2. The current roster's revenue ceiling is ~$2.4M/year.** At 10 active billable staff, 75% utilization, and 100% realization of the card, annualized revenue tops out around $2,410K. At today's operating point (59% utilization, ~74% realization) the same roster produces ~$1.3–1.4M annualized. **The $6M Year-2 goal therefore requires roughly 2.5× today's billable capacity** — utilization and realization fixes get the division to ~$2M+; the rest is hiring and EPC engineering capture. The grid on the Realization tab shows every combination.

**3. Derived OpEx runs ~$76K/month against ~$85K/month revenue.** With gross margin averaging 18% YTD (and negative in March and May), the cost structure only works at materially higher revenue per person. This is the loss-leader mechanics made visible: the fix is throughput (utilization × realization), not cost-cutting alone.

**4. Three org-chart people show no hours in the KPI report** (Tom Little, Erin Bryden, Patrick Nicholson), and two people with hours aren't on the org chart (Taylor Nelson, Kevin Metts — classifications assumed Engineer II and Designer II, flagged orange in the workbook). Roster reconciliation is a Phase 1 exit item.

## Phase 1 exit criteria (open items)

From finance: fringe/benefit load and salaries (for loaded-cost vs bill-rate margin by role), overhead allocation methodology, interest basis, and the transfer-pricing treatment of internal hours. From the team: confirm the two assumed classifications, the VP-time billing treatment, and where the three missing people's time goes. Then decompose the $150K realization gap on the Realization tab.
